extractions.unit: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

extractions.unit: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);

alternative_quotes: makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges)
impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes)
unit_attributes.choice_quote: makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes)

unit_attributes.logic_text: makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant ... or impedes the functioning of facial recognition
unit_attributes.summary: Material damage is defined as any damage to the facial area making the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (such as creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impeding the operation of facial recognition (such as damage around the eyes).

extractions.unit: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes). Immaterial damage is acceptable;

unit_attributes.summary: Immaterial damage—defined as background damage or non-material facial area damage (e.g., staple holes)—is acceptable on the photograph.
